headline: Medium prompt-injection and data-leakage risks arise from shared file-based workflows; Plandex’s write access can amplify Khoj’s retrieved content into unsafe actions.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Khoj reads indexed personal notes/files and can expose retrieved content; Plandex reads and writes the project directory and stdin/stdout. If Khoj content is copied into Plandex prompts or plans, attacker-controlled text in notes can steer downstream instructions. This is not provably blocked by either profile, but the bridge is indirect rather than a shared MCP channel.
conditions: IF Khoj-retrieved note text is pasted into Plandex prompts or plans
IF Plandex auto-applies instructions derived from copied note content
mitigations: Disable auto-apply in Plandex for any task sourced from notes
Paste only quoted excerpts, never full retrieved documents
Add a manual review step before any plan execution
Use a separate scratch file for copied content
requires-engineering: add provenance tags from Khoj into Plandex inputs

B_data_leakage.rationale: Khoj touches personal notes and indexed documents, while Plandex touches source code and can write files in a project directory. A shared workspace or copied context can move sensitive note content into code artifacts or model-provider requests. The profiles do not show a guaranteed shared filesystem, so this is plausible but not proven to be default-safe.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same workspace or copied files
IF note content from Khoj is included in Plandex prompts or generated code
mitigations: Keep Khoj notes and Plandex projects in separate directories
Redact secrets before copying text between tools
Turn off any automatic export of retrieved notes into code files
Review generated diffs for leaked note content before apply
requires-engineering: enforce workspace isolation at the orchestrator

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Plandex can write the filesystem and modify git state, while Khoj reads files and maintains a shared index across clients. If both operate on the same repository or directory, Plandex’s edits can race with Khoj’s indexing and stale reads can occur. The profiles do not show locking or coordination, so overlap is plausible in default use.
conditions: IF Khoj indexes a directory that Plandex is editing
IF Plandex modifies git state while Khoj is reading the same files
mitigations: Pause Khoj indexing during Plandex apply steps
Use separate clones for notes and code
Commit or stash before running Plandex changes
Refresh Khoj’s index after each Plandex apply
requires-engineering: add file-lock coordination between tools

D_cascading_error.rationale: Khoj can surface retrieved notes/documents, and Plandex is a planner that stages changes before apply. If Plandex treats Khoj output as authoritative, a mistaken or malicious retrieval can cascade into code changes or staged actions. Because Plandex can write files and modify git state, the blast radius includes irreversible repository changes.
conditions: IF Plandex uses Khoj output as a source of facts without verification
IF Plandex auto-applies a plan derived from retrieved notes
mitigations: Require source verification before plan creation
Compare Khoj claims against original files or external sources
Keep Plandex in review-only mode for Khoj-sourced tasks
Limit apply permissions to a human-approved diff
requires-engineering: add citation/provenance checks between agents

E_compliance.rationale: Khoj is a personal knowledge manager for notes and indexed documents, while Plandex is a coding tool that handles source code and sends context to model providers. If personal notes contain regulated or residency-sensitive data and are copied into Plandex, the pair can create a policy mismatch. The profiles do not specify HIPAA/GDPR guarantees, so uncertainty pushes this to medium rather than low.
conditions: IF regulated personal notes are copied from Khoj into Plandex
IF the deployment requires residency or retention controls not documented in either profile
mitigations: Do not move regulated notes into Plandex workspaces
Strip personal data before using Plandex
Confirm retention settings for both tools before use
Keep separate accounts or deployments for sensitive data
requires-engineering: document and enforce residency/retention policy
